experiment.claim: Substantiates spec/target-spec.md's DRAFT "Iq (excl. load current)" row (< 30uA at no load and full load) against the LDO core-regulation-loop schematic landed by #14 (design/ldo_3v3in_1v8out.sch), using the row's own two named load points. That row is DRAFT (issue #1 not yet ratified) -- the bound below cites it directly, not an invented final limit, and needs re-verification once #1 rules. Each corner runs two .op solves (0mA then 50mA, via the deck's own 'alter' on the load current source, mirroring sim/loop-gain's multi-point convention from #25): Iq is defined, per design/README.md's own "Iq = total VIN current minus load current" convention, as -i(vvin) at no load (no subtraction needed) and as -i(vvin) minus the deck's own known 50mA load constant at full load. Known risk, not a testbench defect -- and confirmed during this testbench's own bring-up, not just cited from elsewhere: design/README.md's dated 2026-08-25 root-cause section (issue #60, mechanism 1; tracked by #69) documents a thermal-shutdown false-trip at the ff/sf process corners at 125C, independent of load current; a direct check at ff/125C/3.63V (screening, not part of this record) confirms TS_CMP=0.39V (tripped; untripped is approximately VIN) and vout collapsed to -19.2V at full load (0.14V at no load) at that exact corner, yet -i(vvin) itself still reads a plausible-looking, in-budget microamp figure there rather than an obviously non-physical one -- unlike line-regulation/load-regulation, where the same false-trip produces an unmistakably out-of-range number. vout_no_load_v/vout_full_load_v are reported (unbounded) alongside the Iq figures specifically so a reader can see when the underlying operating point is not really regulating (roughly 1.8V) before trusting an in-budget Iq PASS at that corner, per the same PSRR caution design/README.md's mechanism 5 already states ("PASS" at a falsely-tripped corner is not evidence of a genuine pass).
